steps.headline: A picture now has zoom controls in the top-left corner instead of being stuck at whatever size fits.
steps.changed: A small bar with minus, the current size, plus, and a magnifier. The size is also a button — click it to snap back to fitting the pane. Minus is greyed out here because you are already fitted, and hovering it says so rather than leaving you guessing.
steps.measured: This 1600×1000 picture is shown at 15% of its real size — previously with no way to see more
steps.notice: The bar is always there while a picture is open, not only when you hover, so you can find the magnifier without knowing it exists. It sits in the pane's corner, so a small picture is never covered — only one that fills the pane.
steps.risk: Pinching a picture on the trackpad now zooms the PICTURE, where before it zoomed the whole app. Pinching anywhere else still zooms the app exactly as it does today.

steps.headline: With the magnifier on, a lens follows your cursor and makes small print readable without changing the view.
steps.changed: Clicking the magnifier turns on lens mode; moving over the picture shows a circle magnifying whatever is under the cursor. Inside it the text reads 'quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog'; outside it, the same text is a grey smear.
steps.measured: Lens is 180px across at 2.5× the current size; it switches off with Escape or the same button
steps.notice: The picture itself does not move, so you keep your place. The lens hides itself when you leave the picture, and on a picture smaller than the lens it does not appear at all — there would be nothing to reveal.
steps.risk: On a low-resolution picture the lens shows big soft pixels, because there is no hidden detail to find. The magnifier button is not offered on a phone, where there is no cursor for a lens to follow.

steps.headline: The magnifier works on drawings too, and on a drawing it is genuinely sharp rather than just bigger.
steps.changed: The same lens, over a .svg drawing. A drawing has no fixed resolution, so it is REDRAWN at the magnified size instead of being stretched: the small caption inside the circle is crisp. Nothing else about how drawings are displayed has changed.
steps.measured: 6px caption in the drawing: unreadable on the page, legible in the lens
steps.notice: Drawings look exactly as they did before — same size, same position. The only difference is that the magnifier now opens on them at all.
steps.risk: A photo cannot do this. Magnify one far enough and you get bigger pixels, not more detail, which is why the lens stops at 8× a photo's real resolution.
